candidates.lead: Bev Craig says people from across all 10 boroughs had complained to her about potholes
candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor launches £60m pothole repair programme - BBC News Image caption, Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig says the funding will be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road By Mairead Smyth , Reporting from in Eccles and Angela Ferguson , North West Published 47 minutes ago The mayor of Greater Manchester has unveiled a £60m pothole repair programme, saying people from all 10 boroughs had complained to her about the issue. Bev Craig said funding would be made available to all of the boroughs and it would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road. Craig had promised to repair more roads and make sure pavements were safe during her election campaign. But Rod Dennis from the RAC said what was needed to fix "Britain's pothole woes, and those we see in Manchester, is guaranteed long-term funding over many, many years". Image caption, Funding is being made available to all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs Dennis called for "an end to the kind of patch and dash approach which we've seen some councils employ and proper planning to get the roads back to where they need to be". Craig said 2.5 billion journeys were made across the roads of Greater Manchester every year "and we need to properly invest in them and this is about getting money out of the door quickly to fix the things that people have been complaining to me about". Image caption, Garage owner Dave Rigby says that almost every day he sees drivers bring in vehicles damaged by potholes Dave Rigby, who runs a garage in Eccles, told BBC North West Tonight that potholes were "quite a big factor", with vehicles often brought in there every day for repairs as a result of them. He said they could damage a vehicle's suspension as well as damaging tyres and wheel alignment and tracking. "From a business point of view, obviously we do make money off it but, for customers, the cost of living's gone up and stuff, so, obviously, if the roads are better it's more money in people's pockets," he said. 'Common and frustrating' Transport for Greater Manchester said the allocated funding would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road, helping to tackle existing issues and resurface roads and pavements to prevent them from deteriorating in the first place. It said damaged sections of roads and pavements were "a common and frustrating issue affecting drivers across the country", as well as walkers and cyclists. The funding is being divided across all 10 boroughs as follows: Bolton - £6.55m Bury - £4.37m Manchester - £8.16m Oldham - £5.26m Rochdale - £5.24m Salford - £5.39m Stockport - £6.82m Tameside - £4.98m Trafford - £4.99m Wigan - £8.24m Craig said these amounts were worked out using a formula "based on how many roads you've got and the length of roads. Across Greater Manchester 125km of roads exist". She said the way it had been shared out across local authorities was simply "the more roads you have, the more money you get". The extra funding comes from existing transport budgets and follows a national increase in government funding for pothole repairs. candidates.lead: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
candidates.evidence_text: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Six officers were sacked without notice by Greater Manchester Police. By Paul Burnell Reporting from North West Published 2 September 2026 Six serving police officers have been sacked following an internal investigation by Greater Manchester Police into alleged racial discrimination against a fellow officer. GMP said two other former officers who were also investigated would have been fired if they were still on the force. Another officer received written warning. A force disciplinary panel heard the female officer of African heritage (who was not named in the proceedings) complained after her accent was mimicked by a group of officers. She was also compared to a suspect with similar skin colour, while one officer made a derogatory comment about her hair. The panel found six officers and two former officers committed gross misconduct, while a ninth officer was found to have committed misconduct. PCs Demi Green, Heena Rani, Lucy Granby, Matthew Barlow, Matthew Hill, and Mohammed Abid - who made the remark about his colleague's hair - were dismissed without notice. Former PC Jake Holt and another unidentified former officer were also found to have committed gross misconduct. Sgt Adrian Bick, whose actions amounted to misconduct, but who did not breach the force's standard of equality and diversity, received a written warning. Deputy chief constable Terry Woods said: "No officer or member of staff should have to come to work and experience discriminatory behaviour from the people they serve alongside. "I would like to acknowledge the courage of the officer who came forward and reported these concerns. It is important that people have the confidence to speak up, knowing they will be listened to and supported. "Since this investigation began, our Bury district has worked closely with officers, staff and community representatives to listen to concerns, take action, and ensure we remain a police service that our diverse communities can identify with and be proud of." candidates.lead: Allie Pottinger painted a mural for a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room
candidates.evidence_text: I want to give comfort to grieving families, says artist - BBC News Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, Artist Allie Pottinger, with Mandy and Josh Ogden of the Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation, stand in front of the new mural By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 2 September 2026 An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby. Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together. She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope". It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there. Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, Allie Pottinger's first mural - in memory of her father - depicted Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death. "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist. She said: "Nature is very calming - and it is better than looking at white blank walls." Pottinger, who grew up in Macclesfield but now lives in Congleton, said it was "really rewarding" to paint murals at the hospital. Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, The bluebell woods mural in the family room of the critical care unit is one of four artworks Allie Pottinger has painted at Macclesfield General Hospital She said of her latest artwork: "I just want to bring some comfort to people who have lost babies and are in an awful state." Her watercolour was printed, digitalised and installed on the wall at the Bluebell Suite thanks to funding from the Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation. The charity, which aims to help improve the wellbeing of individuals living in Cheshire and Staffordshire, was founded by Georgia's parents, Mandy and Mark, and her brother, Josh, shortly after she died in a car crash in Astbury, Cheshire, in 2020. Mandy Ogden said: "The loss of a child, regardless of their age, is the most devastating news any parent can ever receive. "Sadly, having experienced that heartbreak ourselves at another hospital, one memory that has never left us is receiving that life-changing news in a small, cold, clinical room, which was used for storage." She said that "truly heartbreaking experience" inspired their donation "so that parents at Macclesfield Hospital could receive that news in a peaceful and comforting space, where they could take time to reflect together". She said Allie "has captured that vision perfectly". "Her incredibly beautiful artwork brings tranquillity and hope to a place where they are needed most, and we are deeply grateful for the care and compassion she has poured into her work." 'Calming effects' Francesca Stanley, a bereavement midwife at East Cheshire NHS Trust which runs the hospital, said staff were very grateful to Pottinger for donating her "wonderful work" and the generous donation from the The Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation. She said: "The bluebell mural has been carefully chosen to bring the calming effects of nature into the room, helping to reduce stress and create a comforting environment during an incredibly difficult time." candidates.evidence_text: A mother has told how her family's lives changed over night when her son developed life-threatening sepsis at the age of five Archie, from Wigan, Greater Manchester, was diagnosed with meningitis B which developed into sepsis , external and he spent five days in a coma in 2018 He was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, where he received specialist care and rehabilitation before being discharged two weeks later His mother Kate said her son's illness "changed our lives overnight" and seeing him "so seriously unwell and fighting for his life was the most frightening time we have ever experienced as a family" Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to infection anywhere in the body, where, instead of fighting the bacteria or virus that is making you ill, the immune system turns on itself, damaging internal organs and potentially causing death Now aged 13, Archie continues to receive care at the hospital, attending for regular check-ups, undergoing operations, and receiving physiotherapy and occupational therapy

candidates.evidence_text: An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope" It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope" It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist

candidates.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

And the Environment Agency told the MEN the contamination may be affecting public health In correspondence sent to the Manchester Evening News , an anonymous local resident who claimed to be speaking on behalf of the local community, said a leak had been 'continuously discharging' down Alt Hill Lane in Ashton-under-Lyne for more than 18 months The resident, who said they feared it may be sewage, said the issue had been reported last year but alleged that 'absolutely no action has been taken to isolate the biohazard or protect the public.' They said the main area affected was near the old railway bridge and entrance to the public bridleway on the rural road which sits on the border of Tameside and Oldham The path is a popular route for walkers, dog walkers, children and cyclists and recently it has been 'impossible to cross the road to the opposite path entrance without walking through it' they said

NHS leaders are urging everyone eligible to book their vaccine as soon as they are invited to help reduce demand on services at the busiest time of year Health officials warn winter illnesses, including flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), can be "very serious" for vulnerable people. Vaccination is the "best way to reduce the risk of becoming seriously unwell", they add The NHS says more than two million flu jabs were delivered in the North West last year. Around four million people in the region will be eligible for the flu vaccine this year Pregnant women and children will be offered the flu vaccine from September 1, while older adults, people in care homes, people clinically at risk and health and social care workers will be eligible from October 1

The former GP, now aged 37, underwent a gruelling course of treatment including chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy Despite a setback during treatment, when she developed sepsis, she was eventually given the all-clear. Before the treatment, Annie froze her eggs after being told her fertility could be affected But in 2024, she and her husband Daniel were delighted to find out that they had conceived naturally. Then at 35 weeks, Annie became very unwell again while on holiday in France The couple cut their trip short and travelled back to the UK, reaching her sister's home in Berkshire before she was admitted to hospital. There, she received the devastating news that her cancer had returned and was now stage four

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major update has revealed a surprising new plan for a historic Stockport library that’s been shut for more than a year Stockport Central Library has been closed since May 2025 after maintenance works and repairs had to be carried out in the building. It has remained shut ever since despite petitions and calls for it to reopen Library services in Stockport town centre have since been operating out of the massively popular Stockroom in the Merseyway Shopping Centre. This has had more than one million visitors in a year However the library’s likely future has been revealed after Reform councillor Shaun Regan put in a Freedom of Information request to the local authority He said he had ‘been pressing the council for clear answers’ in a Facebook post because the public ‘deserve to know what is happening to one of our most important public buildings’

english_fact_card.who_affected: Residents of the nearest community south of the site in Wigan borough; Bolton planning committee will determine the application.
english_fact_card.why_now: Wigan Council has formally objected, citing concerns that the transport assessment's traffic generation claims are not credible.

english_fact_card.reader_action: Monitor Bolton Council's planning committee decision; no public deadline is stated.

english_fact_card.what_happened: An NHS trust recorded ten 'never events' across 2025 and 2026, described by the NHS as wholly preventable patient safety incidents. Bosses have been warned to take urgent action to address patient care concerns, and the trust is facing a backlog of hundreds of complaints. More than 350 theatre staff walked out this week in a dispute over overtime payments, leading to a critical incident declaration and cancellation of several hundred patients' operations.
english_fact_card.where: Hospitals in Salford, Oldham, Bury and Rochdale, Greater Manchester
english_fact_card.who_affected: Patients at the affected hospitals; theatre staff (nurses, clinical support workers, housekeepers)
english_fact_card.why_now: Newly published board papers reveal the backlog of complaints and urgent warnings, and industrial action has caused cancellations.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Patients and families using these hospitals should be aware of potential service disruptions and safety concerns.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Check with the hospital or NHS trust for updates on appointments and operations if affected.

candidates.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved while the council has acknowledged it did fail to tell people in advance and apologised . candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Tameside's mystery discharge pouring down road for 18 months 'may be affecting public health' Tameside Council and the Environment Agency are investigating Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 05:56, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 06:43, 03 Sep 20 Locals have spoken out about their concerns as they claim a mystery 'leak' on a road in Tameside has been causing a 'major health hazard' for more year and a half. And the Environment Agency told the MEN the contamination may be affecting public health In correspondence sent to the Manchester Evening News , an anonymous local resident who claimed to be speaking on behalf of the local community, said a leak had been 'continuously discharging' down Alt Hill Lane in Ashton-under-Lyne for more than 18 months The resident, who said they feared it may be sewage, said the issue had been reported last year but alleged that 'absolutely no action has been taken to isolate the biohazard or protect the public.' They said the main area affected was near the old railway bridge and entrance to the public bridleway on the rural road which sits on the border of Tameside and Oldham The path is a popular route for walkers, dog walkers, children and cyclists and recently it has been 'impossible to cross the road to the opposite path entrance without walking through it' they said

candidates.evidence_text: NHS NHS issues 'serious' flu warning as virus could strike earlier than usual this winter The warning comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 21:05, 02 Sep 2026 Vi Health officials have urged millions of people across the North West to protect themselves against winter viruses as the NHS warns flu could strike earlier than usual this winter It comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected, putting pressure on NHS services. NHS leaders are urging everyone eligible to book their vaccine as soon as they are invited to help reduce demand on services at the busiest time of year Health officials warn winter illnesses, including flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), can be "very serious" for vulnerable people. Vaccination is the "best way to reduce the risk of becoming seriously unwell", they add The NHS says more than two million flu jabs were delivered in the North West last year. Around four million people in the region will be eligible for the flu vaccine this year Pregnant women and children will be offered the flu vaccine from September 1, while older adults, people in care homes, people clinically at risk and health and social care workers will be eligible from October 1

While the A Bed Every Night scheme does provide emergency accommodation, there is currently a waiting list and people are having to share spaces which The most common reasons for homelessness are either family or friends no longer willing or able to accommodate people, the end of a private rented tenancy, those leaving Home Office accommodation, and domestic abuse. Her £60m Pothole Fund will go towards repairing around 125km of road in a big effort to tackle the pesky pothole problem The recently elected GM mayor believes this will increase the safety and reliability of the highways network, not just for cars, but for buses, trams and cyclists Sorting out potholes formed part of her mayoral manifesto when campaigning to replace her predecessor, Andy Burnham . Ms Craig pointed out she didn’t need to hear about potholes on the doorstep, she could see the problem with her own eyes when travelling around the city-region Ms Craig said: “I’m investing in making sure our roads are modern, up to standard and getting rid of those potholes. The £60m Pothole Fund is going straight to councils, who will help us do that View 4 Images Bev Craig, mayor of Greater Manchester, stood on Trevor Road in Eccles (Image: TfGM)

Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 18:13, 02 Sep 2026 View 3 Images ( A Salford councillor is planning to challenge the local authority over the controversial decision to approve hundreds of new houses on former greenbelt. Peel Land were given the green light to build 282 ‘high-quality’ homes on land around the RHS Bridgewater in Boothstown in July The controversial decision left people in the area angered and upset. Locals claim the surrounding roads are already ‘at breaking point’ with congestion Conservative councillor Bob Clarke has launched a fundraiser on the community’s behalf to cover legal costs to haul the decision in front of a court of law. More than £14,000 has been raised for the judicial review in under a week, almost a third of the total predicted cost of ar Coun Clarke told the LDRS : “I’m not against housebuilding. But this is about the infrastructure of the entire area, which isn’t ready for that amount of people. It’s not just the roads, it’s the schools, doctors, dentists View 3 Images The land next to the RHS Bridgewater. (Image: Copyright Unknown)

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major update has revealed a surprising new plan for a historic Stockport library that’s been shut for more than a year Stockport Central Library has been closed since May 2025 after maintenance works and repairs had to be carried out in the building. It has remained shut ever since despite petitions and calls for it to reopen Library services in Stockport town centre have since been operating out of the massively popular Stockroom in the Merseyway Shopping Centre. This has had more than one million visitors in a year However the library’s likely future has been revealed after Reform councillor Shaun Regan put in a Freedom of Information request to the local authority He said he had ‘been pressing the council for clear answers’ in a Facebook post because the public ‘deserve to know what is happening to one of our most important public buildings’

All charges relate to the same sin Jury selection has begun at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester today (September 2). A jury of 12 people, five men and seven women, were selected and were sent away until tomorrow. Two alternative jurors, two women, were also selected

candidates.evidence_text: Lancashire Heartbreak as 'much-loved' football coach dies just two weeks after devastating diagnosis "Andy was one of those people who represented everything that is good about grassroots football" News Jon Macpherson and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaki A 'much-loved' Lancashire football coach has tragically died just two weeks after receiving a devastating cancer diagnosis Andrew Lawrenson, known to all as Andy, was told he had stomach cancer last month. Tragically, just two weeks after the diagnosis, he died surrounded by his loved ones on Friday, August 28 He was a beloved secretary and coach at Kirkham Juniors FC and 'gave so much of his time, effort and commitment' to the team, the club said. The club broke the devastating news of Andy's death on Facebook as they paid tribute to him They said he dedicated eight years to the club's committee, serving as its secretary, and was also a committed coach of the Under-15 Reds - a team he had nurtured since their Under-6 days, working alongside fellow coach Graham. In a statement, the club said: "Rest in Peace, Andy "Unfortunately, Kirkham Juniors has a very sad announcement to make. It is with great sadness that we announce the passing of Andrew (Andy) Lawrenson, our club Secretary, a much-loved and long-serving member of our football club

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Wigan blackmailer faces jail over torrent of vile abuse and threats sent to MPs over Palestine Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan, sent threats and blackmail messages to high-profile MPs including Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secreta A Wigan man bombarded Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secretary Sir James Cleverly with a torrent of vile abuse over the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The MPs, plus former Business Secretary Peter Kyle, were left offensive emails and voice mails at their constituenc Over a three-month period, Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan , threatened harassment, made ''defamatory references'' and used ''highly abusive language'' about the MPs. He is also said to have used blackmail in his messages Sir James who quit the shadow cabinet at the weekend to run for London mayor and Labour minister Mr Kyle who served in Sir Keir Starmer's Government before being dismissed by Andy Burnham in July provided victim personal statements about the abuse Prosecutors are currently awaiting a similar statement from Ms Cooper who was previously subjected to a death threat from another social media user not linked to Mr Price. The Speaker of the House of Commons Sir Lyndsay Hoyle has also given prosecutors an ''impactful'' statement At Wigan Magistrates' Court Price pleaded guilty to three charges of sending by public communication network an offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing message or matter

And the Environment Agency told the MEN the contamination may be affecting public health In correspondence sent to the Manchester Evening News , an anonymous local resident who claimed to be speaking on behalf of the local community, said a leak had been 'continuously discharging' down Alt Hill Lane in Ashton-under-Lyne for more than 18 months The resident, who said they feared it may be sewage, said the issue had been reported last year but alleged that 'absolutely no action has been taken to isolate the biohazard or protect the public.' They said the main area affected was near the old railway bridge and entrance to the public bridleway on the rural road which sits on the border of Tameside and Oldham The path is a popular route for walkers, dog walkers, children and cyclists and recently it has been 'impossible to cross the road to the opposite path entrance without walking through it' they said

candidates.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport boss speaks amid chaos as new bin rule which nobody was told about is put in force One Stockport councillor said the controversy was 'a heck of a way to get a lot of feedback from people in a very short space of time' Comments News Stockport council's deputy boss faced questions for the first time after 'Binlid-Gate' sent collections into chaos last month Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved while the council has acknowledged it did fail to tell people in advance and apologised . Last week, the council's Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport. candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Andy Burnham backs MEN campaign to save Jodrell Bank as our petition tops 10,000 signatures Funding cuts threaten the future of the observatory's iconic and much-loved Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope News John Scheerhout C A petition launched by the Manchester Evening News to save space science at Jodrell Bank has now been signed by more than 10,000 people in just five days. candidates.evidence_text: NHS NHS issues 'serious' flu warning as virus could strike earlier than usual this winter The warning comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 21:05, 02 Sep 2026 Vi Health officials have urged millions of people across the North West to protect themselves against winter viruses as the NHS warns flu could strike earlier than usual this winter It comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected, putting pressure on NHS services. NHS leaders are urging everyone eligible to book their vaccine as soon as they are invited to help reduce demand on services at the busiest time of year Health officials warn winter illnesses, including flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), can be "very serious" for vulnerable people. Vaccination is the "best way to reduce the risk of becoming seriously unwell", they add The NHS says more than two million flu jabs were delivered in the North West last year. Around four million people in the region will be eligible for the flu vaccine this year Pregnant women and children will be offered the flu vaccine from September 1, while older adults, people in care homes, people clinically at risk and health and social care workers will be eligible from October 1

The former GP, now aged 37, underwent a gruelling course of treatment including chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy Despite a setback during treatment, when she developed sepsis, she was eventually given the all-clear. Then at 35 weeks, Annie became very unwell again while on holiday in France The couple cut their trip short and travelled back to the UK, reaching her sister's home in Berkshire before she was admitted to hospital. There, she received the devastating news that her cancer had returned and was now stage four

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Surprising new plan for historic Stockport library that's been shut for a year A Reform councillor said the public ‘deserve to know what is happening to one of our most important public buildings’. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major update has revealed a surprising new plan for a historic Stockport library that’s been shut for more than a year Stockport Central Library has been closed since May 2025 after maintenance works and repairs had to be carried out in the building. It has remained shut ever since despite petitions and calls for it to reopen Library services in Stockport town centre have since been operating out of the massively popular Stockroom in the Merseyway Shopping Centre. This has had more than one million visitors in a year However the library’s likely future has been revealed after Reform councillor Shaun Regan put in a Freedom of Information request to the local authority He said he had ‘been pressing the council for clear answers’ in a Facebook post because the public ‘deserve to know what is happening to one of our most important public buildings’

english_fact_card.what_happened: Wigan Council has published a formal objection to a planning application by Keepmoat Homes for 310 homes on green belt land between Hindley and Westhoughton.
english_fact_card.where: The site is in Bolton borough, close to Wigan Road, near a former greyhound stadium at Hewlett Way and Hart Common golf course, and borders Wigan borough.
english_fact_card.when: The objection was published in the week leading up to 2 September 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Residents of the nearest community south of the site in Wigan borough; Bolton planning committee will determine the application.
english_fact_card.why_now: Wigan Council has formally objected, citing concerns that the transport assessment's traffic generation claims are not credible.

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Wigan blackmailer faces jail over torrent of vile abuse and threats sent to MPs over Palestine Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan, sent threats and blackmail messages to high-profile MPs including Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secreta A Wigan man bombarded Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secretary Sir James Cleverly with a torrent of vile abuse over the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The MPs, plus former Business Secretary Peter Kyle, were left offensive emails and voice mails at their constituenc Over a three-month period, Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan , threatened harassment, made ''defamatory references'' and used ''highly abusive language'' about the MPs. He is also said to have used blackmail in his messages Sir James who quit the shadow cabinet at the weekend to run for London mayor and Labour minister Mr Kyle who served in Sir Keir Starmer's Government before being dismissed by Andy Burnham in July provided victim personal statements about the abuse Prosecutors are currently awaiting a similar statement from Ms Cooper who was previously subjected to a death threat from another social media user not linked to Mr Price. The Speaker of the House of Commons Sir Lyndsay Hoyle has also given prosecutors an ''impactful'' statement At Wigan Magistrates' Court Price pleaded guilty to three charges of sending by public communication network an offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing message or matter

The attraction, which ‘no one talks about’ locally, is already bringing in people from across the country Daisy Nook Country Park is a 40 hectare site in the River Medlock valley which sits in both Oldham and Tameside boroughs. Daisy Nook’s history stretches back over 200 years where the canals there acted as a key supplier of coal that powered Manchester’s industrial revolution and The area is known for its beautiful scenery, wildlife, and waterways and is popular with photographers. Later this month, the Friends of Daisy Nook Country Park are set to formally sign an agreement on September 11 to help move an ‘ambitious’ community led programme forward Working with the Hollinwood Canal Society, this will look to restore and regenerate the park. £120,000 of funds is set to be spent over the coming months which will help restore sections of the historic canal and a former boat pond This is on top of work since 2024 to improve paths, create community spaces, tackle invasive species like Japanese knotweed and Himalayan balsam, improve accessibility, and carry out repairs

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.lead: Six officers and two former officers were found to have committed gross misconduct, and a ninth officer found to have committed misconduct, following an internal investigation into alleged racial discrimination against an officer on the Bury district.
candidates.evidence_text: Six officers and two former officers were found to have committed gross misconduct, and a ninth officer found to have committed misconduct, following an internal investigation into alleged racial discrimination against an officer on the Bury district GMP’s Professional Standards Directorate launched an investigation in July 2024 after a report was made that an officer had been subjected to racist behaviour by colleagues in December 2023 Following misconduct proceedings, a panel found that the actions of PC Demi Green, PC Heena Rani, PC Lucy Granby, PC Matthew Barlow, PC Matthew Hill, PC Mohammed Abid, former PC Jake Holt and former Officer A – who has been granted anonymity – amounted to gross misconduct They also found Sergeant Adrian Bick’s actions amounted to misconduct, as there was no breach of the standard of equality and diversity As a result, six serving officers have been sacked without notice, while two former officers would have been dismissed had they not already left the force. Sergeant Bick was issued a written warning The panel heard how PC Y, who has African heritage and has been granted anonymity, made a complaint after her accent was mimicked by a group of officers

As it stands, the planning system makes it far too diffic The analysis shows, city by city, the number of homes to be gained just by matching the density around stations of peer cities in France and Japan. We invite customers to travel with us from Manchester Airport to experience our world class products and service, thoughtfully curated cuisine, and warm hospitality.”. . Flight SQ301 departs Manchester at 1035hr and arrives at award-winning Changi Airport in Singapore at 0700hr the following day. With seamless connections to more than 130 destinations across the combined networks of Singapore Airlines and its low-cost subsidiary Scoot, the early arrival time offers added convenience, particularly for customers travelling onwards.. . The route is operated by Airbus A350-900 long-haul aircraft, which is configured with 253 seats (42 in Business Class, 24 in Premium Economy Class, and 187 in Economy Class). To this, investors, developers, Mill readers and general members of the public Jack Dulhanty of course spent the whole of yesterday evening dialling up his phonebook trying to get the inside story. Councillor for Harpurhey and Christmas Pat Karney told the MEN that the leadership contest was “friendly and orderly,” and assured them that “town-hall drama” wa But first, in case you missed it, we’d like to urgently draw your attention back to Saturday’s article, which asks the question: ever seen those fundraisers in the blue jackets and wondered — is this a scam? Well over the weekend, Lucy, Ophira and Alec put their heads together to write one of our most popular stories of the year: the story of two cigar-smoking, rolex-wearing, quick-tempered salesmen behind the Educate & Empower ‘fundraising’ scheme. We went to visit them in their Sno If you haven’t read it, we hugely recommend you do so here ! And, if you have, our latest podcast may be of interest to you, in which Jack comes back from holiday after missing all the reporting to ask Ophira what really went down behind the scenes. You can listen to that on Spot

Adult social care works with vulnerable adults who have physical, learning disabilities, and mental health needs Last year (2025/26) 9,937 people received long-term adult social care support, which includes support in people’s own homes, as well as support to people in Care Homes, Extra Care schemes and supported living. Another 6,232 were accessing short-term care through services such as Strengths highlighted in the CQC report include timely assessments for most people, with the starting point of all assessments being what is important to the individual and what they want to achieve. Effective early support was also praised as well as good access to support (most The assessment also identified some areas for development, which the Council will be prioritising as part of wider continuous improvement and transformation plans. candidates.evidence_text: Vintage cars, live entertainment, and traditional performances will take over Oldham town centre for a free celebration of all things retro Oldham town centre will turn back the clock on Saturday 19 September, as residents and families are invited to come together for Nostalgic Oldham, a free day of retro entertainment Taking place from 11am to 4pm, the annual event will bring a packed programme of free activities and performances to the town centre, combining traditions, childhood memories, and family fun At the heart of the celebrations will be the return of the Big Yellow Bus in Parliament Square, which will become a hub of activity throughout the day. Visitors can enjoy circus performances, live music, and strolling street entertainment Another highlight of the day will be the official unveiling of a huge community-created mural of Oldham by artist Dave Draws in The Market The large scale illustrated map captures the borough's rich heritage while celebrating modern day Oldham. Local people have helped shape the artwork through drawing, storytelling, and personal connections to the borough

candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: BGF-backed Celerity makes second acquisition in 6 months Posted on September 3, 2026 by staff BGF-backed Celerity makes second acquisition in 6 months Manchester-based IT services firm which swooped for Ranger4 in April now moves for Warwick business Insight 2 Value Share: Deals Celerity, a Manchester-based managed IT services provider backed by investor BGF, has acquired Insight 2 Value (I2V). Based in Warwick, I2V is a specialist in intelligent automation and enterprise content management, with expertise in IBM FileNet and Cloud Pak for business automation. The acquisition will strengthen Celerity’s capacity to provide solutions that improve customer onboarding, complaints handling, case management and regulatory compliance, connecting content seamlessly to improve service delivery and accelerate customer-facing operations. “We’re thrilled to welcome Insight 2 Value to our team. This acquisition means our customers can now benefit from even more powerful solutions – combining intelligent automation and content-driven workflows with our cyber-resilient infrastructure,” said Craig Aston, CEO of Celerity. “Together, we can help organisations streamline their most critical processes, reduce complexity, and ultimately deliver better experiences to their own customers. “This is about giving our customers access to smarter, more integrated tools that tackle the challenges that matter most to your business.” Phil Hagen, managing director of Insight 2 Value, said: “Joining Celerity is a natural next step for Insight 2 Value. We’ve dedicated ourselves to helping businesses simplify experiences and deliver rapid value while mitigating common implementation challenges. “Celerity gives I2V a platform to continue developing market-leading solutions and delivering exceptional client services for organisations of all sizes, whilst working alongside a wider team of exceptional talent and a service portfolio that complements everything we do.” Edinburgh firm pureLiFi crashes into administration Celerity has achieved accelerated growth since receiving a £15m investment from growth capital investors BGF in 2021, which has helped drive service diversification, strategic partnerships and complementary acquisitions. The transaction follows Celerity’s acquisition of Ranger4 in April 2026, taking the business’ headcount to a team of 107. Harry Jones, partner at BGF, added: “This acquisition is an important milestone for Celerity that will further differentiate its service proposition. candidates.lead: Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities.
candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Manager Michael Carrick oversaw a significant midfield rebuild, while the club also planned for the future by snapping up several top prospects United needed to strengthen and add depth to their squad, having finished third and qualified for the Champions League without having to contend with a European campaign last term. Deadline day passed on Tuesday without United welcoming a new left-back It leaves Luke Shaw short of backup or competition for his place in Michael Carrick’s side. The 31-year-old featured in all 38 league games last term but United face a more demanding campaign this time around as they return to the Champions League United held interest in Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall but both targets were unavailable. The Reds were also linked with a move for Barcelona full-back Alejando Balde but no agreement materialised United boss Carrick has preferred to use Patrick Dorgu further forward, while 19-year-old Harry Amass is inexperienced. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. И, возможно, именно эта неожиданная Чтобы попасть на концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте
